narrativeReportMd:
# Condition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking local changes were found. The most important R4-to-R6 validation breaks are mandatory `Condition.clinicalStatus`, the replacement of the R4 `Condition.evidence` backbone with `CodeableReference`, the incompatible entered-in-error status rule, and removal of `ClinicalImpression` as a `stage.assessment` target. The main R6-to-R4 risks are `clinicalStatus=unknown`, native `bodyStructure`, CodeableReference-shaped evidence, and widened actor targets.

## Scope
The analysis compared the supplied base R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition-Condition.json` files and related local terminology/dependency artifacts. Inherited base-resource and datatype changes are explicitly out of scope except where needed to explain a local Condition element.

## Main migration themes
R6 makes Condition status more explicit, especially by requiring `clinicalStatus` and documenting `unknown`. It also adopts newer modeling patterns (`CodeableReference`, native `bodyStructure`) that require JSON and generated-code changes. Several reference target changes affect strict validation and cross-version conversion.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `Condition:CARDINALITY:Condition.clinicalStatus:0d4f73`, `Condition:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Condition.entered-in-error:64d0aa`, and `Condition:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:Condition.evidence:4c8e21`. These can invalidate existing R4 instances or require non-trivial transformation.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for backfilling missing clinical status, handling entered-in-error records, confirming the R6 `unknown` terminology against an external terminology package/server, and deciding whether evidence grouping or causality information is preserved during `CodeableReference` conversion.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some changes appear justified by safety or model consistency, but several could have been staged less disruptively through profiles, extensions, or transitional dual representations. In particular, the entered-in-error rule creates a direct bidirectional incompatibility that should be handled deliberately.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover generic `CodeableReference`, BodyStructure, external HL7 Terminology content for `condition-clinical`, and base Resource/DomainResource inherited deltas.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Condition has material local breaking changes. The top migration concerns are mandatory `clinicalStatus`, the `evidence` CodeableReference rewrite, and entered-in-error incompatibility. The main uncertainty is terminology: the local R6 core package lacks the external condition-clinical CodeSystem needed to verify the full R6 code expansion.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be organized around four workstreams: (1) status normalization and clinical governance for missing or entered-in-error statuses; (2) structural conversion of `Condition.evidence` between R4 backbone and R6 CodeableReference; (3) strict reference-target remediation for `stage.assessment`, recorder, and asserter; and (4) body location conversion between the R4 `bodySite` extension and R6 native `bodyStructure`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level deltas because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for exact terminology code deltas involving R6 `condition-clinical` because the R6 package references an external CodeSystem not present locally and no expansion service was used. Official diff pages and rendered narrative would improve rationale assessment but are unlikely to change the core structural findings.

findings.title: Condition.clinicalStatus is now mandatory

binding.description: The clinical status of the condition or diagnosis.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the condition as no longer active.

semanticText.short: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved
semanticText.definition: The clinical status of the condition.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `Condition.clinicalStatus` could be omitted. The resource-level warning `con-3` encouraged it for problem-list items, but omission was still valid for many Conditions, including point-in-time encounter diagnoses and entered-in-error records.

binding.description: The clinical status of the condition or diagnosis.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains codes that mark the condition as no longer active.

semanticText.short: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved | unknown
semanticText.definition: The clinical status of the condition.
semanticText.comment: clinicalStatus is required since it is a modifier element. For conditions that are not problem list items, the clinicalStatus may be unknown.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `Condition.clinicalStatus` must be present on every Condition. The R6 comment explicitly explains that the field is required because it is a modifier and points to `unknown` for non-problem-list use cases.

facts.oldValue: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved
facts.newValue: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved | unknown

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, path, type, and modifier meaning are unchanged; the material delta is the minimum cardinality increase.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for R4-to-R6 migration: an R4 Condition without `clinicalStatus` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. Runtime impact is high because generated models, validators, serializers, ETL pipelines, and business rules that treated the field as optional must now always supply it. The R6-to-R4 risk is medium because ordinary R6 clinical status codes are structurally representable in R4, but R6's documented use of `unknown` is not in the local R4 complete CodeSystem.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Clinical status affects whether a problem is active, inactive, resolved, or otherwise clinically relevant. Backfilling an incorrect status can alter decision support, problem-list displays, and quality reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure every Condition carries an explicit modifier status so consumers do not accidentally treat status-unknown records as active or valid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep clinicalStatus optional in base R6 while adding unknown, clearer absence semantics, and profile or best-practice requirements for workflows that need explicit status.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is clinically credible: `clinicalStatus` is a modifier, and requiring either a known status or `unknown` reduces the chance that consumers silently treat absent status as active or resolved. The less-breaking design would avoid invalidating R4 data, but it would not give base R6 consumers a uniform guarantee that status is present. Because that safety tradeoff is material, the base break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `Condition.clinicalStatus` at `0..1`, added `unknown`, clarified that absence means status is not known or not applicable to the workflow, and used a warning, invariant, or profile to require status for problem-list or safety-critical use. That preserves old instances but weakens the universal modifier-status guarantee that R6 appears to be pursuing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances but leaves missing modifier status base-valid and relies on profiles or warnings for safety-critical uniformity.

evidence.detail: R4 minimum cardinality is 0.
R6 minimum cardinality is 1.
R6 explains that clinicalStatus is required because it is a modifier and that non-problem-list conditions may use unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally small and isolates the missing `clinicalStatus`; a complete production transform must choose a clinically justified status rather than defaulting everything to `unknown`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Condition.clinicalStatus` changed from optional to mandatory. This is the highest-impact local Condition change because it can invalidate otherwise well-formed R4 instances that omitted status. The R6 model appears to prefer explicit uncertainty (`unknown`) over absence, which is safer for consumers but requires migration policy and possibly manual clinical review for historical data.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation can fail solely because `clinicalStatus` is absent. R6-to-R4 conversion is usually possible for the six R4 clinical status codes, but R6 content using `unknown` is not valid against the local R4 complete CodeSystem and required binding. Strict enum-based clients must also add support for the new required value and for the fact that the element is never absent in valid R6 base instances.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 Conditions with missing `clinicalStatus`. Derive a status only when business rules are clinically sound, for example from problem-list state or abatement; otherwise use a deliberate `unknown` policy for R6 and document that this cannot round-trip cleanly to base R4. Test omitted status, active/inactive/resolved statuses, abated Conditions, and entered-in-error Conditions separately.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The safety goal is credible because modifier status changes interpretation of the resource. The backward-compatible alternative would have been to keep the base optional and require status through profiles, but that would preserve the R4 ambiguity that R6 appears to be addressing.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for migration defaults. Treating all missing R4 statuses as `unknown` may be technically valid in R6 but can change analytics and workflow behavior.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a Condition without clinicalStatus, while R6 requires clinicalStatus 1..1 and explicitly provides unknown for non-problem-list or point-in-time conditions such as claims-derived records. This is a real old-valid/new-invalid validation and generated-model break for systems that omitted status, but the affected element is a modifier and the R6 goal of making status or uncertainty computable is clinically coherent. A migration can often use a policy-driven unknown value when the status is genuinely unavailable, though problem-list data should not be blindly defaulted.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Condition.clinicalStatus min=0, max=1, isModifier=true, required binding to condition-clinical|4.0.1.
R4 root con-3 was warning-level and only encouraged clinicalStatus for problem-list items outside entered-in-error cases.
R6 StructureDefinition Condition.clinicalStatus min=1, max=1, isModifier=true, and comment says clinicalStatus is required because it is a modifier; non-problem-list conditions may use unknown.
R4 Condition is supplied as FMM 3/trial-use; R6 Condition metadata is FMM 5/normative, but this review applies the supplied R4 maturity context.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use raises compatibility expectations for this central clinical resource but is not a normative freeze; the safety rationale for mandatory modifier status carries substantial weight.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Condition omitting clinicalStatus can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6; generated models and serializers also move from optional to required.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could have kept clinicalStatus optional and used a warning, invariant, or profiles for workflows needing explicit status. That would preserve R4 instances but would not give base R6 consumers a uniform computable modifier-status guarantee.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact assessment and partially agree with its partial-alternative judgment; the break is real, but the modifier-status rationale makes it proportionate rather than a Revisit.

findings.title: Condition.clinicalStatus required binding now documents an `unknown` status

oldState.summary: R4 required binding points to condition-clinical|4.0.1; the local complete CodeSystem has six codes and no `unknown`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 package includes `CodeSystem-condition-clinical.json` with complete content: active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, and resolved.

semanticText.short: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved

oldState.narrativeMd: R4's locally available complete CodeSystem did not include an `unknown` clinical status code.

newState.summary: R6 required binding points to condition-clinical|6.0.0-ballot4; the StructureDefinition short/comment explicitly include `unknown`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 core package does not include the external THO CodeSystem, so `unknown` is inferred from the R6 Condition element short and comment rather than from a local expansion.

semanticText.short: active | recurrence | relapse | inactive | remission | resolved | unknown
semanticText.comment: For conditions that are not problem list items, the clinicalStatus may be unknown.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 documents `unknown` as part of the clinical status value space and recommends it for some non-problem-list Conditions.

facts.note: Inferred from R6 Condition.clinicalStatus short/comment; local R6 package lacks the external CodeSystem expansion.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element and required binding canonical are used, but the local package does not contain the R6 terminology CodeSystem needed to verify the full code delta.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 status codes remain plausible in R6, so this is not an R4-to-R6 validation break by itself. The risk is R6-to-R4 and runtime: an R6 instance using `unknown` does not validate against the local R4 complete CodeSystem, and enum-based R4 clients may reject or mishandle it.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A status of `unknown` is clinically different from active, inactive, or resolved; collapsing it to an older code can mislead users.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide a computable status when R6 requires clinicalStatus but the clinical state is genuinely unknown.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding documented `unknown` status widens the R6 clinicalStatus value space and does not remove the R4 clinical status codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not an R4-to-R6 old-valid/new-invalid break by itself. Once R6 requires `clinicalStatus`, a computable `unknown` value is a reasonable way to distinguish true uncertainty from active, inactive, resolved, or absent status. The verdict remains probable rather than absolute because the local R6 package did not include the external CodeSystem expansion.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is needed to preserve R4 instances: existing R4 status codes remain acceptable. Using a data-absent-reason extension or keeping status optional would be a different modeling choice and may help R6-to-R4 conversion, but those are not backward-compatible base-design alternatives for an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 enum and down-conversion policy remains necessary, but avoiding `unknown` would weaken R6 handling of mandatory status when the clinical state is genuinely unknown.

evidence.detail: R4 short lists six clinical status codes and not `unknown`.
R4 local complete CodeSystem contains active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, and resolved.
R6 short includes `unknown`.
R6 comment says non-problem-list conditions may have a clinicalStatus of unknown.
The R6 ValueSet includes all codes from the external condition-clinical CodeSystem, but that CodeSystem was not present in the local core package.

examples.examplesMd: The example is R6-oriented and assumes the external R6 terminology includes `unknown`, as indicated by the R6 StructureDefinition text.

findings.narrativeMd: R6's required clinical status model introduces a documented `unknown` status. That is not a problem for R4-to-R6 validation of existing known statuses, but it is a concrete round-trip and code-generation risk because the local R4 required value set/code system does not include `unknown`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R6 Condition using `clinicalStatus=unknown` is expected to be valid in R6, but it is not valid under the local R4 complete `condition-clinical` CodeSystem. Strict R4 validators and generated enum types will reject it unless they are configured with cross-version mappings or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, decide whether `unknown` should be omitted, represented with an extension, mapped to a local code, or cause a conversion warning. Omission is not lossless because R6 deliberately distinguishes unknown status from absent status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified as a complement to mandatory clinicalStatus. The backward-compatible alternative would have been preserving optionality or using an extension for uncertainty; both make R6 less uniform for consumers.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm the exact R6 `condition-clinical` code list against the matching HL7 Terminology package or terminology server before making production enum changes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The specific terminology change is an added documented clinicalStatus value, unknown. It does not make any R4 clinicalStatus code invalid in R6, so it is not an R4-to-R6 breaking change by itself. It matters for R6-to-R4 conversion and enum-based clients, but those are downstream/reverse concerns created by new R6 content rather than a base design problem for preserving R4 instances.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition short lists active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, and resolved.
R4 local CodeSystem condition-clinical is complete and contains active/inactive with nested recurrence, relapse, remission, and resolved; no unknown code is present.
R6 StructureDefinition short lists active, recurrence, relapse, inactive, remission, resolved, and unknown.
R6 ValueSet condition-clinical includes the external condition-clinical CodeSystem but the local R6 package does not include a complete CodeSystem expansion.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use means compatibility still matters, but this is a widening/addition rather than an old-valid/new-invalid change, so maturity does not create a reason to revisit it.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 Condition using clinicalStatus=unknown will not validate against the supplied R4 required value set/code system, but existing R4 statuses remain acceptable in R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable: adding unknown is the less-breaking way to support mandatory status when the real clinical status is unavailable; avoiding it would force misleading mappings or absence.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing no-hard-break assessment but disagree with treating the finding as medium impact for this fresh R4-to-R6 judgment; the alternative judgment is effectively not applicable.

findings.title: Entered-in-error Conditions changed from forbidding clinicalStatus to requiring it

oldState.summary: R4 had an error constraint `con-5` forbidding clinicalStatus when verificationStatus is entered-in-error.

constraints.human: Condition.clinicalStatus SHALL NOT be present if verification Status is entered-in-error

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, an entered-in-error Condition with `verificationStatus=entered-in-error` had to omit `clinicalStatus` to satisfy `con-5`.

newState.summary: R6 removed the entered-in-error exclusion and makes clinicalStatus mandatory for all Conditions.

constraints.human: If condition is abated, then clinicalStatus must be either inactive, resolved, or remission.
constraints.expression: abatement.exists() implies (clinicalStatus.coding.where(system='http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-clinical' and (code='inactive' or code='resolved' or code='remission')).exists())

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no local root constraint equivalent to R4 `con-5`; because `clinicalStatus` is 1..1, even entered-in-error Conditions must carry a clinical status.

facts.note: The cardinality change makes the removed R4 constraint impossible to preserve as-is.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is a root-level local Condition constraint in R4. R6 root constraints were compared and no entered-in-error counterpart was found.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The two versions impose incompatible validation expectations for entered-in-error Conditions. R4 accepts and effectively requires omitted `clinicalStatus` in this case; R6 requires `clinicalStatus`. A mechanically valid R6 entered-in-error instance with clinicalStatus will violate R4 `con-5`, while the R4 form without clinicalStatus violates R6 cardinality.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Entered-in-error records are uncommon but safety-relevant because consumers must not treat erroneous Conditions as active problems.

justification.inferredGoal: Make clinicalStatus uniformly present even for modifier/error states.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 entered-in-error exception by making clinicalStatus conditionally required only when verificationStatus is not entered-in-error.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Uniform `clinicalStatus` is a reasonable R6 goal, but the entered-in-error state already has explicit modifier semantics through `verificationStatus`. R4 required the opposite shape for that state, so R6 creates a direct cross-version incompatibility without local rationale for why the exception had to disappear. A narrow conditional exception would have preserved old records with modest tradeoff, making this break probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could keep `clinicalStatus` at `0..1` and add an invariant requiring it unless `verificationStatus` is `entered-in-error`, while documenting how consumers should interpret error records. That still advances explicit-status safety for ordinary Conditions and avoids forcing erroneous records to carry a potentially misleading clinical status.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The exception slightly reduces uniformity and requires conditional validation, but it preserves the established error-state shape and avoids bidirectional invalidity.

evidence.detail: R4 has an error invariant forbidding clinicalStatus when verificationStatus is entered-in-error.
R6 root constraints include the abatement rule and bodyStructure/bodySite rule but no entered-in-error clinicalStatus exclusion.
R6 clinicalStatus minimum cardinality is 1.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example satisfies the old entered-in-error rule by omitting clinicalStatus. The R6 example demonstrates why a valid R6 representation cannot be made base-R4-valid without dropping or relocating clinicalStatus.

findings.narrativeMd: The entered-in-error case is not merely affected by the general cardinality increase; the versions disagree about the correct shape. R4 says clinicalStatus SHALL NOT be present when verificationStatus is entered-in-error, while R6 requires clinicalStatus and drops the R4 exclusion. This creates a real bidirectional conversion problem for erroneous records.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6: an entered-in-error Condition that omits clinicalStatus is invalid in R6. R6-to-R4: an entered-in-error Condition that includes clinicalStatus is invalid in R4. This affects validators, cross-version transforms, and business logic that uses entered-in-error as a deletion/error marker.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Handle entered-in-error Conditions as a special migration case. For R4-to-R6, add a policy-driven clinicalStatus, likely `unknown` if confirmed by R6 terminology. For R6-to-R4, remove or extension-map clinicalStatus when verificationStatus is entered-in-error and record the loss of information. Add tests specifically for entered-in-error records with and without clinicalStatus.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This incompatibility was probably avoidable by preserving an exception in R6 or defining a sanctioned cross-version extension. Because neither appears in the local StructureDefinition, conversion requires local policy.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A clinical governance decision is needed before defaulting an entered-in-error record to any clinical status. The safest conversion may be workflow-specific.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 and R6 impose opposite shapes for entered-in-error Conditions. R4 has an error invariant forbidding clinicalStatus when verificationStatus is entered-in-error; R6 removes that exception while requiring clinicalStatus for every Condition. This creates a direct bidirectional validation conflict for records whose explicit purpose is to mark an erroneous condition, and adding a clinical status to an entered-in-error record can be semantically awkward or misleading.
keyEvidence: R4 root constraint con-5 is severity=error and expression requires clinicalStatus.empty() when verificationStatus coding is entered-in-error.
R6 root constraints include the abatement rule and bodySite/bodyStructure mutual exclusion, with no entered-in-error exclusion.
R6 Condition.clinicalStatus has min=1, so an entered-in-error Condition still requires a clinicalStatus.
R4 verificationStatus remains a modifier because refuted and entered-in-error mark the Condition as not currently valid.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use raises the burden for introducing an avoidable direct validation conflict, especially on a modifier/error-state path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 entered-in-error Condition without clinicalStatus is invalid in R6; the R6 form with clinicalStatus is also not base-R4-valid under con-5.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: R6 could keep clinicalStatus 0..1 with an invariant requiring it unless verificationStatus is entered-in-error, preserving the R4 error-state exception while still requiring explicit status for ordinary Conditions. The tradeoff is one conditional rule and less uniformity, but the compatibility and semantic benefits are strong.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact assessment and agree with its Yes/probably-avoidable alternative judgment.

findings.title: Condition.evidence changed from a BackboneElement with code/detail to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Repeating BackboneElement with child arrays `code` and `detail` and invariant con-2 requiring at least one of them.

constraints.human: evidence SHALL have code or details

semanticText.definition: Supporting evidence / manifestations that are the basis of the Condition's verification status, such as evidence that confirmed or refuted the condition.
semanticText.comment: The evidence may be a simple list of coded symptoms/manifestations, or references to observations or formal assessments, or both.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented each evidence item as a local backbone component. Codes appeared at `Condition.evidence.code[]` and references at `Condition.evidence.detail[]`, and one evidence component could group multiple codes and multiple references.

newState.summary: Repeating CodeableReference<Resource> with concept/reference substructure supplied by the datatype.

semanticText.definition: Supporting evidence / manifestations that are the basis for determining the Condition.
semanticText.comment: Do not use Condition.evidence for causality... The evidence may be a simple list of coded symptoms/manifestations, or references to observations or formal assessments, or both.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 replaces the local component with the cross-version-new `CodeableReference` datatype. In JSON, coded evidence moves to `evidence[].concept`; referenced evidence moves to `evidence[].reference`.

facts.newValue: removed because the local backbone no longer exists

facts.oldValue: code bound by example to manifestation-or-symptom
facts.newValue: evidence CodeableReference bound by example to clinical-findings

facts.note: R4 marked evidence child elements summary; R6 marks the CodeableReference element itself summary.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 element has the same path and clinical purpose but uses a different datatype and removes the R4 child element identities.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard serialization and validation break. R4 JSON with `evidence.code` or `evidence.detail` is not shaped like R6 `CodeableReference`, and R6 JSON with `evidence.concept` or `evidence.reference` is not shaped like R4's backbone component. Generated classes and accessors also change substantially.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Evidence can justify confirming or refuting a diagnosis. A lossy transform can separate evidence concepts from the observations/reports they were grouped with.

justification.inferredGoal: Use the standard CodeableReference pattern for elements that can be either a concept or a resource reference.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 evidence backbone and add an optional CodeableReference-based representation or transitional child while deprecating code/detail.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of using the standard `CodeableReference` pattern is reasonable and aligns Condition with a broader R6 modeling style. A dual or transitional model could reduce breakage, but it would create two same-resource representations for the same evidence fact and would not cleanly resolve R4 grouping of multiple codes and details versus `CodeableReference` items. Those material tradeoffs make the alternative only partial and the breaking redesign probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could preserve `Condition.evidence.code` and `Condition.evidence.detail` for one release while adding a new CodeableReference form. That would let R4-shaped instances validate, but validators, search logic, FHIRPath, serializers, and consumers would need precedence and consistency rules between old and new forms, and deprecated evidence paths might accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old JSON for common cases but duplicates evidence representations, complicates grouping and validation, and risks deprecated paths persisting indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 evidence is a BackboneElement with con-2.
R4 has `evidence.code` as 0..* CodeableConcept with an example manifestation-or-symptom binding.
R4 has `evidence.detail` as 0..* Reference(Resource).
R6 evidence is 0..* CodeableReference targeting Resource and bound by example to clinical-findings.
CodeableReference has `concept` and `reference` children, each 0..1.

examples.examplesMd: A common R4 transform is to split each `evidence.code` item into a CodeableReference with `concept` and each `evidence.detail` item into a CodeableReference with `reference`. If an R4 evidence backbone grouped multiple codes and details, that grouping may not be preserved.

findings.narrativeMd: `Condition.evidence` was remodeled from a resource-specific backbone component to `CodeableReference`. This is a major local representation change: paths, generated types, validation, and FHIRPath expressions all change. The clinical intent is similar, but the old child identities `evidence.code` and `evidence.detail` are gone.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `evidence.code` or `evidence.detail` are invalid against the R6 structure. R6 instances with CodeableReference-shaped evidence are invalid against R4 unless transformed. Generated client code that expected `ConditionEvidenceComponent.getCode()` or `getDetail()` must switch to `CodeableReference.concept` and `reference`. Summary-mode behavior may also change because R6 marks `Condition.evidence` itself as summary.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Implement an explicit bidirectional transform. For R4-to-R6, map each `evidence.code` to `evidence.concept` and each `evidence.detail` to `evidence.reference`; preserve grouping only if your target model and downstream logic can represent it. For R6-to-R4, map `concept` back to `code` and `reference` back to `detail`, with warnings if a single CodeableReference contains both or if grouping semantics matter. Update FHIRPath, JSONPath, serializers, and generated model tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change aligns with a reusable R6 datatype and is probably justified for model consistency. A less disruptive alternative would have kept the R4 backbone for one version and added a parallel CodeableReference element, but that would introduce duplicate ways to say the same thing.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review migration rules for causality separately. R6 adds text warning not to use Condition.evidence for causality; the appropriate extension or AdverseEvent path may be workflow-specific.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Condition.evidence changed from a resource-specific backbone with code[] and detail[] children to a repeating CodeableReference<Resource>. That is a real wire-format and generated-API break: old JSON paths evidence.code and evidence.detail are gone, and R6 uses concept/reference under the datatype. The R6 design is nevertheless coherent because this is exactly the CodeableReference use case, and retaining both the old backbone and the new datatype would duplicate evidence representations and require conflict rules.
keyEvidence: R4 Condition.evidence is 0..* BackboneElement with error constraint con-2 requiring code or detail.
R4 Condition.evidence.code is 0..* CodeableConcept bound by example to manifestation-or-symptom.
R4 Condition.evidence.detail is 0..* Reference(Resource).
R6 Condition.evidence is 0..* CodeableReference targeting Resource and bound by example to clinical-findings.
R6 CodeableReference has concept 0..1 CodeableConcept and reference 0..1 Reference.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use makes the serialization break important, but the content is still trial-use and the reusable datatype goal is a proportionate R6 modeling improvement.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 evidence.code/detail JSON is not the R6 CodeableReference shape; generated accessors and FHIRPath expressions also change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial: R6 could retain the R4 backbone for a transition while adding a CodeableReference form, but that would create duplicate same-resource evidence representations, precedence questions, and potentially indefinite support for the old shape. Grouping of multiple R4 codes/details still needs migration policy either way.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing high-impact assessment and its partial less-breaking alternative judgment.

findings.title: Condition.stage.assessment no longer allows ClinicalImpression references

oldState.summary: Reference target profiles allowed ClinicalImpression, DiagnosticReport, and Observation.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 staging assessments could point to a ClinicalImpression as a formal assessment supporting the stage.

newState.summary: Reference target profiles allow DiagnosticReport and Observation only.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 removes ClinicalImpression from the allowed targets while keeping DiagnosticReport and Observation.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same element path and cardinality; only the Reference target profile set changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 Condition whose stage assessment references a ClinicalImpression is invalid in R6 because the target profile was removed. R6-to-R4 is low risk for this element because R4 accepts the remaining R6 targets.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Stage information can drive oncology and chronic-disease management; losing a formal assessment reference can reduce clinical traceability.

justification.inferredGoal: Constrain stage assessment evidence to report or observation resources rather than broader clinical impressions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep ClinicalImpression in the base target list and discourage or profile it out where R6 wants only Observation or DiagnosticReport evidence.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of focusing stage assessment on Observation or DiagnosticReport evidence is plausible, but the supplied inputs do not show why `ClinicalImpression` had to be removed from the base target set. Retaining the old target while adding clearer guidance or profiles would preserve R4 instances and still allow narrower R6 implementations. Because the compatibility cost is direct and the less-breaking alternative is straightforward, the base narrowing was probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base R6 design could keep `ClinicalImpression` as an allowed `stage.assessment` target, mark it as discouraged in narrative, or constrain it out in oncology or implementation-specific profiles. Unlike duplicating an element, retaining a reference target mainly leaves the base resource broader; it does not create competing same-resource fields for the same fact.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A broader target list slightly weakens semantic consistency but preserves old references with low implementation burden and no duplicate data shape.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles include ClinicalImpression, DiagnosticReport, and Observation.
R6 target profiles include DiagnosticReport and Observation only.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative. A real transform needs a clinically valid replacement Observation or DiagnosticReport, not just a changed reference string.

findings.narrativeMd: `Condition.stage.assessment` was narrowed by dropping ClinicalImpression as an allowed reference target. This can break R4 staging data that used a ClinicalImpression as the formal assessment record.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A reference to `ClinicalImpression/...` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6 at reference-target validation time. The element cardinality and path are unchanged, so systems that do not validate reference targets may still parse the instance but will be non-conformant.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Find Conditions with `stage.assessment` references to ClinicalImpression. Decide whether the ClinicalImpression should be transformed into or linked through an Observation or DiagnosticReport, or whether a profile/extension is needed to preserve the original reference. Include reference-target validation in migration tests.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The same modeling goal could have been achieved less disruptively by retaining ClinicalImpression in the base target list and constraining it out in profiles. Without rationale, the base-level narrowing is not clearly justified from compatibility alone.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 narrows Condition.stage.assessment by removing ClinicalImpression as an allowed reference target while retaining DiagnosticReport and Observation. A Condition whose stage assessment points to a ClinicalImpression can therefore be valid in R4 and fail R6 reference-target validation. The supplied evidence does not show why the base resource needed this narrowing rather than guidance or profiles, and retaining the target appears to have low structural cost.
keyEvidence: R4 Condition.stage.assessment target profiles are ClinicalImpression, DiagnosticReport, and Observation.
R6 Condition.stage.assessment target profiles are DiagnosticReport and Observation only.
The path, cardinality 0..*, and definition as a formal record of assessment are otherwise materially stable.
Stage assessment can be clinically relevant for disease staging traceability.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use means direct target-list narrowing on a mature clinical resource needs a clear rationale; none is evident in the local inputs.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Condition.stage.assessment reference to ClinicalImpression is no longer allowed by the R6 target profile set.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes: R6 could keep ClinicalImpression in the base target list and discourage or profile it out where a narrower evidence model is desired. The tradeoff is a broader base target set, but it avoids invalidating existing references without duplicate fields.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium/hard-break impact assessment and agree with its Yes/probably-avoidable alternative judgment.

findings.title: R6 adds native Condition.bodyStructure and forbids using it with bodySite

oldState.summary: No native Condition.bodyStructure element; R4 bodySite was CodeableConcept 0..* and its comment pointed to the standard bodySite extension for BodyStructure references.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could represent a detailed BodyStructure reference using the standard extension `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/bodySite`, but not as a native Condition element.

newState.summary: New optional native Reference(BodyStructure) element, 0..1, with a root invariant disallowing simultaneous bodySite and bodyStructure.

constraints.human: bodyStructure SHALL only be present if Condition.bodySite is not present

semanticText.definition: Indicates the body structure on the subject's body where this condition manifests itself.
semanticText.comment: Should be consistent with Condition.code. Cannot be used if Condition.bodySite is used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 gives BodyStructure references a first-class element and adds a local invariant that prevents carrying coded `bodySite` and referenced `bodyStructure` together.

facts.note: The R4 package contains StructureDefinition-bodySite with valueReference BodyStructure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: This is an added element, not a rename of `Condition.bodySite`; R6 keeps `bodySite` and adds `bodyStructure` with a mutual-exclusion invariant.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The addition is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because R4 instances do not contain the native element and `bodySite` remains. The risk is R6-to-R4 and runtime/codegen: R6 instances can use a native `bodyStructure` that R4 base Condition does not understand, and R6 forbids simultaneously sending `bodySite` and `bodyStructure`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Anatomical location can be clinically important, especially where laterality or detailed body structure identification affects interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Promote the common bodySite extension pattern to a native Condition element and clarify coded-vs-referenced location representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 keeps `bodySite` and adds optional native `bodyStructure`, so R4 base Condition instances remain valid unless a migration chooses to promote extension data.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Promoting the existing BodyStructure-reference pattern to a native optional element is a reasonable R6 modeling improvement, and it does not invalidate ordinary R4 Condition instances. The mutual-exclusion rule affects R6 authoring and cross-version conversion choices, but the reported break is mainly R6-to-R4 representability rather than old-valid/new-invalid base validation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Continuing to use only the R4 extension would be more R4-like but would forgo the discoverability and validation benefits of a native R6 element. Because the R6 element is optional and `bodySite` remains available, no less-breaking base R6 design is needed for preserving R4 instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 mapping still needs the bodySite extension, and R6 producers must choose between coded bodySite and BodyStructure, but this is not an R4-to-R6 preservation problem.

evidence.detail: R4 bodySite comment says to use the standard bodySite extension when BodySite resource attributes are needed.
R4 standard bodySite extension carries a Reference to BodyStructure.
R6 adds Condition.bodyStructure 0..1 Reference(BodyStructure).
R6 adds an error invariant disallowing bodyStructure when bodySite exists.

examples.examplesMd: For R6-to-R4, the closest base-compatible preservation strategy is the R4 standard bodySite extension. If an R6 instance also needs a coded bodySite, a single base R6 Condition cannot carry both because of `con-4`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `Condition.bodyStructure` as a native BodyStructure reference. This is mainly a round-trip and generated-model change, not an old-instance break, but it matters because R4 used an extension for this information and R6 adds a validation rule that chooses either coded bodySite or referenced bodyStructure, not both.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Conditions remain R6-valid with respect to `bodySite` as long as they do not introduce `bodyStructure`. R6 Conditions containing native `bodyStructure` are not base-R4-representable without moving the reference to an extension. An R6 Condition containing both `bodySite` and `bodyStructure` is invalid under R6 `con-4` even though an R4 extension-based representation could potentially carry both. Strict code generators need a new property.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, consider promoting `extension(url=bodySite).valueReference` to `Condition.bodyStructure` and remove or reconcile any simultaneous coded `bodySite`. For R6-to-R4, map native `bodyStructure` to the standard R4 bodySite extension. Test cases should cover code-only, bodyStructure-only, and attempted combined representations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The native element is probably justified because it formalizes an existing extension. The breaking aspect could have been reduced by retaining extension guidance and allowing both coded and referenced location with a consistency invariant, but that would allow more ambiguity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional native Condition.bodyStructure and keeps Condition.bodySite. Ordinary R4 Conditions remain valid with respect to this change, and R4 BodyStructure-reference data can still exist as an extension unless a migration elects to promote it. The new R6 invariant requiring bodyStructure only when bodySite is absent affects R6 authoring and mapping choices, but it is not an R4-to-R6 base preservation problem.
keyEvidence: R4 has no native Condition.bodyStructure; Condition.bodySite remains 0..* CodeableConcept.
R4 Condition.bodySite comment points to the standard bodySite extension when BodyStructure attributes are needed.
R4 StructureDefinition-bodySite extension value[x] is 1..1 Reference(BodyStructure).
R6 Condition.bodyStructure is 0..1 Reference(BodyStructure).
R6 root constraint con-4 says bodySite.exists() implies bodyStructure.empty().
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use was considered, but the change is additive for R4-to-R6 compatibility; maturity does not turn a reverse-only/native-model addition into a revisit issue.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: native R6 bodyStructure must be mapped to an R4 extension for downgrade, and R6 forbids combining native bodyStructure with bodySite; there is no old-valid/new-invalid base break for ordinary R4 instances.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for R4 preservation: R6 keeps bodySite and makes bodyStructure optional. Allowing both native fields might aid some mappings but would introduce duplicate coded-versus-referenced location semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-risk description but disagree that it is a meaningful fresh R4-to-R6 problem; the not-applicable alternative assessment is appropriate.

findings.title: Condition.recorder and Condition.asserter allow additional R6 reference targets

oldState.summary: Recorder and asserter both allowed Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 limited both actor fields to human or role actors.

newState.summary: Recorder adds Group; asserter adds Device and Group.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits a Group as recorder and permits Device or Group as asserter, widening who or what can record/assert a condition.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element paths and cardinalities remain; only the Reference target profile sets were widened.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 break because widening accepts all old targets. It is a round-trip and runtime risk because R6 instances may reference target resource types that R4 base Condition does not allow, and older client code may assume recorder/asserter are person-like actors.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Actor provenance affects accountability. Misclassifying a device or group as a person can distort audit trails.

justification.inferredGoal: Support team/group recording and device-asserted Conditions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R6 widens recorder and asserter target profiles, preserving all R4-valid actor references.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing group or device actors reflects plausible recording and assertion workflows, and the change does not reject existing R4 actor references. The remaining costs are runtime assumptions in R6 consumers and representability when converting new R6 content back to R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Using Provenance or extensions for Group and Device actors would help downgrade to R4, but it would be a mitigation for R6-to-R4 conversion, not a necessary alternative to preserve R4 instances in the R6 base model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Closed-union clients and R6-to-R4 conversion need handling for Group and Device, but that is a down-conversion issue rather than a less-breaking R6 base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 recorder targets are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 recorder adds Group.
R4 asserter targets are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 asserter adds Device and Group.

examples.examplesMd: Either the Group recorder or Device asserter is enough to make the instance fail R4 reference-target validation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 widens actor references: `recorder` can now be a Group, and `asserter` can now be a Device or Group. This is useful expressivity but creates cross-version and generated-code risk for systems that assumed these fields always referenced people or roles.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: All R4-valid recorder/asserter targets remain valid in R6. R6 instances using the new targets are not valid base R4 Conditions. Strict validators catch this through target profile validation; looser parsers may accept the reference string but application logic may fail when resolving an unexpected resource type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, map Group/Device actor information to Provenance, an extension, or a local profile if preservation is required. Update R6 client code and UI labels to avoid assuming every recorder or asserter is a person.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative would have kept the base targets unchanged and used Provenance or extensions for group/device actors. Native targets are cleaner for R6 but not round-trip safe to R4.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 widens actor targets: recorder adds Group, and asserter adds Device and Group. This preserves every R4-valid recorder and asserter reference target, so there is no R4-to-R6 instance break. Older code that assumes only person-like actors may need updating for new R6 content, but that is a normal consequence of a compatible target-list widening.
keyEvidence: R4 Condition.recorder targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 Condition.recorder adds Group to the R4 target list.
R4 Condition.asserter targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 Condition.asserter adds Device and Group to the R4 target list.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use supports checking runtime assumptions, but widening the target set does not violate the maturity expectation for preserving R4 instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances using Group or Device actors cannot be represented as base R4 Condition actor references, but R4-to-R6 validation is widened.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable: no less-breaking R6 base design is needed because the change is additive. Using Provenance or extensions instead would improve downgrade behavior but would be a mitigation rather than a better R4-preserving base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse/runtime risk description but disagree with treating it as medium impact for fresh R4-to-R6 compatibility; the not-applicable alternative assessment is appropriate.

findings.title: Condition.category binding weakened from extensible to example

oldState.summary: R4 binding strength was extensible to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category.

binding.description: A category assigned to the condition.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4's extensible binding meant systems were expected to use the standard problem-list-item or encounter-diagnosis category codes when applicable, while still allowing other codes when necessary.

newState.summary: R6 binding strength is example to the same canonical ValueSet.

binding.description: A category assigned to the condition.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 treats the same category ValueSet as only an example, reducing base conformance pressure to use those standard category codes.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element identity is unchanged; only binding strength and descriptive text changed materially.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Weakening a binding is not a hard instance-breaking change; it makes R6 validation less restrictive. The risk is semantic/conformance drift: systems and profiles that relied on the R4 extensible binding may see more varied category coding in base R6 data.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Category often drives problem-list versus encounter-diagnosis workflows; looser base conformance can affect filtering and reporting if profiles do not restate expectations.

justification.inferredGoal: Reduce over-constraining category coding in the base resource.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is to avoid over-constraining category coding in the base Condition resource. That is a plausible design choice and it does not create an R4-to-R6 validation break, though it may increase semantic variation unless profiles restate stronger expectations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is needed for R4 instance preservation because the R6 binding is weaker. Implementations that need R4-like category consistency can reintroduce extensible or required bindings in profiles or validation policy, but that is not a less-breaking base R6 design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: weakening the category binding from extensible to example relaxes base validation and does not invalidate R4 category codings.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the extensible binding would improve uniform category guidance, but the tradeoff is conformance strictness and semantic consistency rather than preservation of old R4 instances.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is extensible.
R6 binding strength is example.

examples.examplesMd: No invalidating JSON example is provided because weakening the binding does not make old instances invalid. The issue is downstream variability, not base validation failure.

findings.narrativeMd: `Condition.category` moved from an extensible binding to an example binding. This lowers base conformance expectations and may increase coding variation in R6 data. It is notable for migration planning because category codes are commonly used to distinguish problem-list items from encounter diagnoses.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by this change; if anything, R6 base validation is less restrictive. Runtime systems that assumed category codings would preferentially use the standard ValueSet may need profile-level validation or broader code handling in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: If your workflow depends on `problem-list-item` or `encounter-diagnosis`, restate category expectations in R6 profiles, validation rules, or terminology services. Do not rely on base R6 binding strength to enforce the R4 extensible behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because this is a weakening, backward compatibility for existing instances is not the concern. The design tradeoff is between flexibility in base R6 and interoperability around common category semantics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 weakens Condition.category from an extensible binding to an example binding on the same value set. That relaxes base validation rather than invalidating existing R4 category codings. It may reduce base-level pressure to use problem-list-item and encounter-diagnosis consistently, but implementations that require those categories can restate the rule in profiles or validation policy.
keyEvidence: R4 Condition.category binding strength is extensible to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category.
R6 Condition.category binding strength is example to the same value set canonical.
Condition.category cardinality and datatype remain 0..* CodeableConcept.
The R4 short text listed problem-list-item and encounter-diagnosis; R6 short text is broader classification wording.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 3/trial-use makes category semantics worth noting, but the base change is less restrictive, so the maturity context does not support a breaking-change concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: semantic/documentation: the conformance expectation is relaxed and may allow more coding variation, but there is no old-valid/new-invalid mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable: weakening a binding is already compatibility-preserving for R4 instances. Keeping extensible would improve uniform guidance but is not needed to avoid breakage.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low/no-hard-break impact assessment and agree with its not-applicable alternative judgment.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. The status changed from draft to active and is listed as a notable non-breaking governance change.
All local cardinalities other than `Condition.clinicalStatus` and the removed R4 evidence children remained materially stable. The clinicalStatus cardinality change is captured as a finding.

Choice type domains for `onset[x]` and `abatement[x]` remain dateTime, Age, Period, Range, and string. Primitive/complex types for identifier, code, bodySite, subject, encounter, recordedDate, severity, stage.summary, stage.type, and note remain materially stable. Evidence and reference-target changes are captured as findings.

The stage rule requiring summary or assessment remains materially unchanged, and the abatement rule remains an error with equivalent inactive/resolved/remission logic despite key/text changes. Removed entered-in-error logic and new bodySite/bodyStructure logic are captured as findings.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on Condition elements in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changes were found for Condition elements.

`clinicalStatus` and `verificationStatus` remain modifier elements with materially the same modifier reasons. R6 explicitly sets `isModifier=false` on many other local elements, which is not a semantic change from the R4 default.
No local Condition differential slicing changes were found.

Binding strengths and ValueSet canonicals were checked. Material binding changes are captured for `clinicalStatus`, `category`, and evidence. Exact code-level comparison is limited by missing terminology expansions and missing R6 external CodeSystems.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Condition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Artifact publication status does not directly change instance validation shape. It is governance-notable because downstream implementers may treat active content as more stable than draft R4 content.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not infer that all R6 deltas are backward-compatible from the status change; the local structural findings still require migration work.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Onset and abatement comments add ambiguity guidance
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The choice type sets and cardinalities for onset and abatement did not materially change. R6 adds explanatory text about ambiguity when Condition.code changes granularity over time.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Business rules should be reviewed if they assumed onset or abatement always applies to the current code granularity rather than a prior representation of the condition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Condition.stage.summary example ValueSet compose is broader in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding strength remains example, so base validation does not require codes from either compose. Without a terminology expansion, this is notable but not a hard compatibility issue.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology services and UI picklists may expose additional stage concepts in R6; profile authors should constrain if they require a narrower set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 evidence text warns not to use Condition.evidence for causality
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The warning text does not itself invalidate instances, and the structural evidence rewrite is already captured as a finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers who used R4 evidence to imply cause should review R6 guidance to use AdverseEvent causality, precoordination, or the condition-dueTo extension where appropriate.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Condition.evidence` depends on CodeableReference. This report covers the local Condition use, but generic datatype-level migration and base datatype changes belong to the CodeableReference/DataType analysis.
R6 adds `Condition.bodyStructure` as a native BodyStructure reference. BodyStructure's own R4-to-R6 breaking changes should be assessed separately before relying on lossless conversion.

The local R6 package references an external condition-clinical CodeSystem and documents `unknown`; exact code-level compatibility needs the matching HL7 Terminology package or terminology server expansion.
Inherited snapshot/base changes were intentionally excluded from local Condition findings and should be handled by the assigned base-artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official generated R4-to-R6 Condition diff or committee change note was available in the local inputs. The report relies on direct StructureDefinition comparison and local related artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official R6 ballot Condition diff/change notes and reconcile any stated rationale with these findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology expansion service was used. SNOMED-based ValueSets and external HL7 Terminology CodeSystems could not be fully compared at the code level.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run expansions using the exact R4 and R6/THO terminology dependencies, especially condition-clinical, condition-category, body-site, clinical-findings, manifestation-or-symptom, and condition-stage.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 core package contained `ValueSet-condition-clinical.json` but not a local `CodeSystem-condition-clinical.json`. The `unknown` code finding is therefore based on R6 Condition element text, not a local complete CodeSystem artifact.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Load the matching HL7 Terminology package referenced by the R6 ValueSet narrative and compare the complete condition-clinical CodeSystem.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local core package Condition example instances were found by searching for `resourceType: Condition`, so prevalence estimates are based on model knowledge rather than local examples.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review implementation datasets, example bundles, or published test fixtures to quantify how often affected patterns occur.
